events.title: Habsburg conquest after White Mountain
hints: A rebel king's army was routed in about two hours outside Prague in 1620.
Noble estates were confiscated and Protestants forced out.
events.summary: After the Battle of White Mountain in November 1620, the Habsburgs executed rebel leaders in 1621, confiscated the estates of Protestant nobles and imposed a new constitution in 1627. Many Protestants were forced to convert or emigrate.

events.title: Munich Agreement and annexation of the Sudetenland
hints: A conference of four powers in September 1938 decided a country's fate without it.
Border fortifications and industrial regions were ceded.
events.summary: At the Munich Conference of 29–30 September 1938 France, Britain and Italy agreed to Germany's annexation of the Sudeten borderlands. The country was not invited, and the loss included fortifications and industrial areas.
events.quip: A famous example of settling a dispute by giving someone else's land to the person making the most noise.

events.title: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
territoryNames: the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
hints: Troops marched into Prague in March 1939, and a protectorate was declared.
The village of Lidice was destroyed in 1942 as reprisal for an assassination.
events.summary: German troops occupied the remainder of the Czech lands in March 1939 and set up a protectorate. Czech industry and workers were put at the service of the German war economy, universities were closed in 1939 and reprisals such as Lidice followed the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich.

events.title: Communist coup and Soviet satellite
hints: A February 1948 coup placed a one-party regime under Moscow's wing.
Uranium from the Jáchymov mines was sent east.
events.summary: After the communist coup of February 1948 the country became a close Soviet satellite. Uranium from Jáchymov was supplied to the Soviet Union, with prisoners used as forced labour in the mines.

events.title: Warsaw Pact invasion
hints: A reform movement named after a season promised 'socialism with a human face'.
Four Warsaw Pact armies crossed the border overnight, while one member refused to take part.
Tanks entered Prague on the night of 20 to 21 August 1968.
events.summary: On 20-21 August 1968 an estimated 250,000 Warsaw Pact troops, led by the Soviet Union and joined by forces from Poland, Bulgaria and Hungary, invaded Czechoslovakia to end Alexander Dubček's Prague Spring reforms. About 137 Czechoslovak civilians were killed during the occupation.

events.title: Stationing of Soviet troops
hints: A treaty signed in October 1968 described a foreign army's presence as temporary.
The garrison, known as the Central Group of Forces, numbered tens of thousands of troops.
The last units went home in June 1991.
events.summary: A treaty of October 1968 provided for the 'temporary stationing' of Soviet troops after the invasion. The Central Group of Forces remained in Czechoslovakia until the last units left in June 1991.
events.quip: 'Temporary' turned out to mean twenty-three years.
